WoW: Forever

Warlock

Warlock levels with a demon tanking for you. Forever split damage curses into Banes, so you now hold one Bane and one Curse at the same time, and Life Tap gives twice the mana it used to.

WoW: Forever · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Written for levelling, 1 to 60. Forever's beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Warlock build has been tested. The longest anyone has played is a level-38 demo. Ability training levels below come from foreverchanges.pro's reading of the beta client.

Is Warlock for you?

Play Warlock if you do not mind tracking a pet, a handful of timers and two resources at once.

Strengths

  • A permanent pet that tanks, from the Voidwalker class quest at 10, with its own threat spell TormentTormentTalent · Rank 1 of 6CastInstantCost20 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown5 sec cooldownTaunts the creature, increasing the chance that it will attack the Voidwalker.
  • Life TapLife TapLevel 6 · Spell · Shadow · Rank 1 of 6CastInstant trades health for mana, scales with Spirit, and gives about double what it gave in Classic
  • A free mount at 40 and a free epic mount at 60, with no gold cost

Weaknesses

  • Five things to track at once: timers, pet, health, mana and shards
  • Demon abilities are trained from Grimoires, bought separately from your own spells, and every rank costs gold
  • Soul shards still do not stack

New to this class?

Is the rotation simple? Three timed effects, a Curse, then filler.

Is it forgiving? The Voidwalker takes the hits, and Drain LifeDrain LifeLevel 14 · Spell · Shadow · Rank 1 of 6CastInstantCost55 ManaRange20 yd rangeDuration5 secTransfers 10 health every 1 second from the target to the caster. Lasts 5 sec. turns your damage back into health.

What carries you while levelling? A demon tanks for you from level 10, and Life TapLife TapLevel 6 · Spell · Shadow · Rank 1 of 6CastInstant turns health into mana, so downtime is short.

Does it need a group? No. The demon covers the tank role, and Create HealthstoneCreate HealthstoneLevel 10 · Spell · Shadow · Rank 1 of 5Cast3 sec castCost95 ManaCreates a Minor Healthstone that can be used to instantly restore 120 health. Conjured items disappear if logged out for more than 15 minutes. at 10 gives you your own emergency heal.

Which demon, when

  • Imp, levels 2 to 10: it "can run out of Mana quickly", and only Demonology's Demonic EnergiesDemonic EnergiesTalentCastInstantYou heal your pet for 15% of all spell damage you deal. When you gain Mana from Life Tap, your summoned demon gains 100% of the Mana you gain. answers that.
  • Voidwalker, from 10: "your tanky option and the best option to use once you unlock it", and beta reports say it "generated an extremely high amount of threat" through its threat spell TormentTormentTalent · Rank 1 of 6CastInstantCost20 ManaRangeMeleeCooldown5 sec cooldownTaunts the creature, increasing the chance that it will attack the Voidwalker., though Wowhead flags that Torment is noticeably weaker until you train rank 2 at 20.
  • Succubus, from 20, as your damage pet: measured at roughly a quarter of your total damage, and it "deals insanely high damage compared to the other available demons." Keep the Voidwalker for elites: beta reports call it "the safest demon to use while leveling."
  • Felhunter, from 30, for Spell Lock and Devour Magic.

Demonic SacrificeDemonic SacrificeSpell · ShadowCastInstantRange100 yd rangeWhen activated, sacrifices your summoned Demon to enhance the opposing aspect of your power, granting you an effect that lasts 7200 sec. The effect is canceled if any Demon is summoned. Imp: Increases your Shadow damage by 15%. Voidwalker: Restores 2% of your total Mana every 4 sec. Succubus/Incubus: Increases your Fire damage by 15%. Felhunter: Restores 3% of your total Health every 4 sec. inverted its buffs and now lasts two hours: sacrificing the Imp gives +15% Shadow, and the Succubus gives +15% Fire. The Classic muscle memory is backwards.

Which race

Read this section in proportion — our own reading, which no source scores: race sits behind spec, gear and knowing your rotation. No race is a wrong answer for levelling — Icy Veins calls the field too close to rank and says the races are close in terms of damage. Warlock has five playable races in Forever: Human and Gnome on the Alliance, Orc and Undead on the Horde, plus the newly playable Troll. The racials that break crowd control are PvP tools: Will of the ForsakenWill of the ForsakenTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownInstantly removes all Charm, Fear and Sleep effects. (Undead, fear, sleep and charm), Escape ArtistEscape ArtistTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration3 secInstantly escape the effects of any movement impairing effect and gain immunity to those effects for 3 sec. (Gnome, roots and snares) and Will to SurviveWill to SurviveTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownInstantly removes all Stun effects. (Human, stuns). That a free trinket slot is worth more than any damage racial below is our own reading; no source compares them.

Only works on Humanoid or Undead corpses within 5 yds. Any movement, action, or damage taken while Cannibalizing will cancel the effect. restores 7% health and mana every 2 seconds for 10 seconds off a nearby Humanoid or Undead corpse, close to 35% of each over its full duration. Horde: Orc. Blood FuryBlood FuryTalentCastInstantCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases Attack Power and Spell Power by 10% for 15 sec. now gives +10% spell power. Shatter CurseShatter CurseLevel 1 · TalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownDuration8 secInstantly removes and grants immunity to all Curses and Banes, and reduces all Magical damage taken by 15% for 8 sec. is new: it strips your own Curses and Banes, grants brief immunity to them, and cuts magic damage taken by 15% for 8 seconds. Note Forever deleted Command, the pet-damage racial that was the entire reason Orc was the Classic Warlock pick. Its racials now point at your own spell damage rather than your pet's.

Horde: Troll is new to Warlock. Quality of life

  • Soul shards got better but not fixed. They are now classed as a Reagent, and Forever added a reagent bag slot, so your soul bag no longer eats one of your four real bags. They still do not stack.
  • Four class quests, all mandatory: Imp at 2, Voidwalker at 10, Succubus at 20, Felhunter at 30. They are short and they are how you get your demons.
  • Tailoring and Enchanting. Tailoring makes your bags including the soul bag, and Enchanting makes the wand Wowhead says "deals more DPS than Shadow Bolt" at this level.
  • Budget for Grimoires: demon abilities are trained from Grimoires, separately from your own spells, and every rank costs gold.
  • The Legacy System hands out extra talent points from world exploration, on top of your level-based points. Wowhead puts the cap at 7 legacy points before level 25, worth 2 extra talent points, enough to reach one tier further than your character level alone would allow. Those points cannot be spent at 20 as printed. Blizzard's Known Issues list opening the Legacy System before level 25 as a bug — the “Y” hotkey works and throws LUA errors on tabs 1 and 3 — so read these as what to spend Legacy points on from 25, not as part of a level-20 build.
  • Demons take a Move To order now. Icy Veins flags it as a real quality-of-life addition: a 100-yard-range command that repositions your pet on demand, instead of relying on Follow and Stay.
  • Aggressive Mode is back, in the pet tab of your spell book, so your demon can be set to engage on its own instead of waiting on an Attack order every pull.

At level 60

Unknown. Nothing about level-60 Warlock is known: no build, no gearing, no rotation, no spec ranking. Raids open December 9.
